page: The Microsoft Azure B2s_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources comprise one physical core with two execution threads, providing 2 burstable vCPUs paired with 8.0 GB of memory (a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio). The configuration includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, alongside vector acceleration via AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance does not feature dedicated GPUs or included local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on remote network storage for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate adequate single-threaded performance alongside constrained multi-threaded execution resulting from the dual-thread single-core topology. The instance recorded a single-core Geekbench score of 1596.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1889.18, both falling in the middle tier of comparable cloud hardware. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 28.38 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks placed in lower percentiles, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 1881.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2993.91, and multi-core stress-ng of 1932.68. Memory bandwidth measured 14.1 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 13.38 GB/sec for writes, contributing to 1.99 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.37 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

Defined by its burstable CPU allocation and lean hardware footprint, the B2s_v2 provides a cost-effective operational profile for variable or low-intensity processing. It reliably handles baseline background compute with the capability to burst during brief load spikes. Primary workload matches include development and staging environments, low-traffic web applications, lightweight background task workers, and low-concurrency microservices. Sustained parallel computing, large database systems, and heavy continuous compilation are restricted by the single-core shared resource ceiling.
description: The Microsoft Azure B2s_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine designed for entry-level and intermittent workloads. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, it provisions 2 vCPUs from a single hyperthreaded physical core alongside 8.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on remote volumes for block storage. In benchmark evaluations, the B2s_v2 achieves middle-tier single-threaded output, scoring 1596.0 in Geekbench and 1889.18 in stress-ng single-core tests. However, overall multi-core compute throughput and memory bandwidth reflect the limitations of its single physical core and burstable CPU credit allocation. With low sustained multi-threaded performance and 3.37 GB/sec static web serving throughput, the B2s_v2 is architecturally aligned with low-traffic web servers, development environments, staging sandboxes, and low-frequency batch processes.
